findings.title: The controller registration deadline is inert after the first registration (pre-existing; the corrective pass's doc wording overstates it)
findings.evidence: b_stuckBootResume.naturalStateAttempt: with the previous incarnation's claim still in state.roles (nothing ever deletes the controller claim — the only `delete this.deps.state.roles[token]` sites are worker paths; identical on main@origin), retireAndRespawnStuckController returns at `if (this.deps.state.roles[token]) return;` (processes.ts 1674/1676; main 1665/1667) and ensureController's alive branch cancels the deadline for the same reason. A resumed pane that hangs during boot is therefore neither killed nor resurrected at the deadline; a pane that dies is recovered only by the next 404'd wake or resync (which did resume with --resume, so B2's transcript loss is fixed). A resumed pane that hangs ALIVE forever would strand the controller until someone kills the pane — same on main.
findings.impact: The spec's Errors row ('dead on probe -> respawns with --resume') holds. The sentence added to packages/daemon/src/daemon/AGENTS.md in this PR ('a registration deadline that elapses on a pane already dead resurrects it at once, and one that elapses on a live-but-unclaimed pane kills it first') is only true for the very first boot in a daemon's life (or after an operator clears the claim). Not introduced by this change; the architect decides whether to fix here (e.g. clear the controller claim when the pane is found dead / on respawn) or route it separately.

findings.title: bash-hook grant stacking now hits the controller TUI (pre-existing hook behaviour, docs/solutions/legion/worker-pane-shell-gotchas.md section 1)
findings.evidence: Per-bash-call count of injected `export LEGION_GRANT=` lines in the controller transcript: already 2 at 14:37:36Z in round 1 (head 0f3edc92, before any session switch), 2-3 through most of round 2, then 2,3,4,5,6 on consecutive calls at 17:47-17:49Z; every UUID is fresh (minted by the hook, not copied by the model). Only one redeems; the controller's `legion gh` calls 403'd `Invalid or expired grant` on two of three attempts during the READY probe and on all attempts during the 3(c) dry run, after which it minted a grant by hand from $LEGION_CONTROLLER_SECRET_FILE and went off investigating instead of answering. Hook registration is once per extension instance and the pane's OMP log shows one instance, so the multiplication is inside the host's hook dispatch, not this branch's session_switch handlers (which register no hooks). grant-prelude-analysis.txt.
findings.impact: The controller is the merge queue: a `legion gh -- pr merge` can 403 and need a retry, and a controller that works around it by reading the secret file is one step from exposing it. Not a regression of #961; worth its own issue.
